results.problem: Ordinal optimization with exact pairwise comparisons, one selected design, alignment level one
results.quote: For every classical comparison budget smaller than the number of designs, we prove that a knockout among uniformly sampled designs attains the optimum.

results.problem: Quantum ordinal optimization with coherent pairwise comparisons
results.bound: rank law polynomial degree at most \min(2q, n-1)
results.previous_best: degree at most q for classical algorithms
results.quote: its rank law w_t=Pr[x_I=t], t\in[n], is independent of the order and satisfies w_t=p(t) for a polynomial p of degree at most min(2q,n-1).

results.problem: Quantum ordinal optimization with one comparison
results.bound: Q_1(n,r) = \frac{r}{n} + \frac{r(n-r)}{n(n-1)}\zeta, \text{ where } \zeta \text{ is the smallest positive root of } F_{n,r}(z) = 2nhz^3 + 3(nk-h^2)z^2 - 4(2n-3)hz - 6mk

results.problem: Selecting the best design with one quantum comparison
results.bound: Q_1(n,1) = \frac{3(n-1) + \sqrt{13n^2 - 18n + 9}}{2n^2}, \quad nQ_1(n,1) > 3 = nC_2(n,1) \text{ exactly when } n > 9
results.quote: The equivalent blind-pick size nQ_1(n,1) increases with n toward (3+\sqrt{13})/2 \approx 3.3028, and for n \ge 3, nQ_1(n,1) > 3 = nC_2(n,1) exactly when n > 9, with equality at n = 9.

results.problem: Quantum ordinal optimization with fixed good-enough fraction
results.quote: Then \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} Q_1(n,r_n) = F_1(\varrho) = \varrho + \varrho(1-\varrho)\zeta(\varrho), where \zeta(\varrho) is the smallest positive root of H_\varrho(z) = 2(1-2\varrho)z^3 + 12\varrho(1-\varrho)z^2 - 8(1-2\varrho)z - 6 = 0.
